review: Independent static review of half-filled exclusion-current feasibility screen
scope: Source/plan reading and syntax/JSON parsing only. The screen was not imported or executed. No scientific outcomes exist in this review and no source was modified.

checks.elliptic: Correct use of m=k^2 with scipy elliptic functions, b=4K/E, a^2=m b^2, Pi/H quadrature, absolute eta, one-period root and SCGF. Flat and critical branches have the correct normalization. The endpoint clamp only tolerates root-roundoff on the specified physical interval; no change to microscopic rates is made.
checks.spatial_functional: The minimized cost is minus the D=1 stationary SCGF after optimizing current. z=sin(phi) gives the displayed secant-squared average and plain phi-gradient energy. All signs and factors are correct.
checks.analytic_gradient: Differentiating the onsite cosine term, periodic nearest-neighbor squared differences and inverse-H current term gives the implemented gradient. Periodic edge differences have no centered-derivative checkerboard null.
checks.constraints: mean(sin(phi))=0 enforces half filling; its Jacobian cos(phi)/N is correct. Orthogonal removal of that normal gives the correct equality-constrained first-order residual. The angle bounds keep density approximately 1e-8 from zero and one; the subsequent interior-margin gate is stricter.
checks.independence: All three prescribed seeds are independent of the elliptic profile. Each is initialized afresh at each grid/case. The direct objective, derivative and constrained optimizer do not call the elliptic oracle. Fourier interpolation followed by a new doubled-grid objective and mass calculation is a useful discretization check.
checks.count_and_grouping: Six prediction cases plus six controls, each on two grids and three seeds, gives exactly 72 attempted spatial optimizations. The two source-error groups include all three prediction biases at their field and exclude controls. They use ordinary raw-value relative L2 error, without baseline subtraction.
checks.provenance_and_limits: The report hashes source and plan, refuses to overwrite an existing report, retains each completed seed result, and enforces a 600-second alarm. The time-limit path saves an unresolved status before raising. D scaling and rate positivity are analytic identities, as stated, not new microscopic computations.
checks.plan_alignment: The 64/128 quadrature pair, 201-point root-map check and edge-gradient discretization are explicit preexecution choices. No field, bias, control, group or separation-threshold drift was found. Exact-anchor precision concerns the elliptic/flat formulas; direct spatial comparisons remain at 0.2%.

interpretation_limits: No strict monotonicity proof is supplied; the sampled root map and independent optimization are numerical diagnostics.
A passing screen validates sampled consistency of the published stationary half-filled branch, not unrestricted global optimality or a continuous parameter domain.
A failed optimization, refinement or budget gate is not a physical failure.
The original quarter-filled proposal review is unchanged.
next_action: Freeze these reviewed source/plan bytes and execute the single declared bounded screen. Retain every outcome and stop under the fixed gates. A pass supports only the later domain/reference assessment.

preexecution_revision.note: The findings arose from the initial source read; the final hashes below identify the corrected bytes. No separate pre-correction snapshot is asserted.

resolved_findings.finding: The candidate filter uses only optimizer success and mass error. It can select the highest SCGF with a failed bound-margin or projected-gradient check even when another seed is admissible. The final gate catches this, so it cannot create a false pass, but it can cause an unnecessary unresolved result and does not fully implement the stated admissible-selection policy.
resolved_findings.fix: Before max selection require finite profile/value, success, mass, interior margin and normalized projected-gradient gates. Preserve all rows and rejection reasons. Keep doubled-mesh error and doubled mass as independent checks of the selected profile rather than selecting on reference agreement.

resolved_findings.finding: A single screen_fail status covers both numerical/reference failure and insufficient ordinary separation. The detailed gate dictionary preserves the distinction, but the top-level status does not.
resolved_findings.fix: Use a numerical_unresolved status if any numerical/reference gate fails; use insufficient_separation only when those gates pass and the source-error margin fails; retain screen_pass for all gates passing.

resolved_findings.finding: The bias-equation residual is saved but never checked by a declared gate. Independent objective agreement protects the value, so this is not an algebra blocker.
resolved_findings.fix: Add a plan/source residual gate consistent with the declared zero-current endpoint tolerance, such as absolute residual <=1e-5. Do not claim the root equation was checked unless this gate is included.

final_checks.selection: Finite value/profile, success, mass, interior margin and projected-gradient residual are now required before maximizing SCGF. Every attempted row remains retained. Missing admissible candidates become null, and all dependent numerical gates fail safely.
final_checks.independent_doubled_mesh: Doubled-mesh value and mass are checked after selection; profiles are not selected by agreement with the elliptic answer.
final_checks.branch_residual: Every saved elliptic case/order residual must be below the declared 1e-5 absolute tolerance.
final_checks.classification: Numerical/reference gate failures now produce numerical_unresolved. The insufficient_separation status requires all numerical gates to pass. The plan matches this distinction.
final_checks.syntax: Python AST and JSON parsed without importing or executing the screen
